messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English that introduces an adult character through behavior and interaction rather than listing physical traits or personality labels. Let the reader learn what the character is like from what they say, notice, and do. Keep the introduction natural and avoid exposition dumps.

Jordan arrived five minutes early and immediately moved the extra chair out of the doorway.

“You know nobody asked you to do that,” Alex said.

“It was in the way.”

“It was fine.”

Jordan looked at the chair, then at the narrow doorway.

“It was not fine.”

Alex laughed. “Okay.”

Jordan set her bag down and noticed the crooked picture hanging above the couch.

“You still haven't fixed that.”

“I like it crooked.”

“You don't.”

“I do today.”

Jordan reached up and straightened it anyway.

“There.”

Alex watched her. “Do you ever leave anything alone?”

“No.”

“That explains a lot.”

Jordan dropped onto the couch. “You invited me over.”

“I know.”

“So technically, this is your fault.”

Alex smiled. “Fair.”

Jordan glanced toward the kitchen. “You have food?”

“Somewhere.”

“That's not an answer.”

“There's cereal.”

Jordan nodded. “Good enough.”

Alex shook her head. “You really do make yourself at home.”

“I've had practice.”
